system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:26 UTC, the proxy logged a successful CONNECT to desktop.dropbox.com with the user agent DropboxUpdate/199.4.6287. The record shows tunnel traffic, but does not establish a file transfer.

At 14:16 UTC, a Sysmon registry event recorded an Explorer UserAssist entry for ivy.chen whose ROT13-encoded path decodes to C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe. This supports that PowerShell was launched at some point, but does not establish what it did or link it to the reported 13:40 window.

The evidence includes SMB activity from WS-ICHEN-01 to DC-NWD-01, with the DC logging a network logon for the workstation computer account; these records do not establish remote administration or command execution.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor status says both winsec and Sysmon were not collected on WS-ICHEN-01 from 13:30 through 14:10 UTC due to a collection outage. This overlaps the reported PowerShell window, leaving a critical process-telemetry gap.
Proxy and network-connection telemetry was available, but does not identify the endpoint process responsible for the reported activity.
The available records do not include a direct PowerShell process-creation event or command line for the reported time.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell appeared at approximately 13:40 UTC, or whether the UserAssist entry at 14:16 UTC is related to the ticket.
What command, script, or interactive action PowerShell performed, and whether it caused any changes or accessed data.
Whether the Dropbox connection involved a user-initiated transfer, an installed updater, or any malicious activity.
Whether the observed SMB activity was part of normal workstation activity or related to the reported PowerShell window.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover endpoint process telemetry for WS-ICHEN-01 during 13:30–14:10 UTC, including EDR data or any retained Sysmon and Windows Security logs.
Collect PowerShell Operational logs, PowerShell history if available, and relevant endpoint artifacts such as Prefetch and UserAssist context to identify PowerShell execution time and behavior.
Review software inventory and endpoint telemetry for Dropbox components, and obtain proxy transaction detail sufficient to determine whether any file-sharing activity occurred.
Correlate with IT patching records and the approved remote-patching workflow to determine whether any activity on WS-ICHEN-01 was IT-initiated.
